JPM.rationale: JPM presents a strong fundamental case: Q1 2026 showed accelerating revenue (+10% YoY to $49.84B), faster EPS growth (+17.2% YoY to $5.94), and stable ~40%+ operating margins. The franchise is elite — #1 in deposits, IB fees, credit cards, and active asset management flows — with ROTCE of 23% well above peer norms. Valuation is compressed: PE at 14.1x sits near the bottom of its 12-month range (13.5x–17.8x) despite improving earnings, and the 7.1% earnings yield offers a 269bp premium over 10-year Treasuries. The stock has essentially flatlined over six months while EPS grew 17%, creating a meaningful disconnect. Offsetting factors temper conviction: leverage expanded from 12.4x to 13.5x assets/equity, the yield curve is flattening (T10Y2Y at 0.49%, down 34% in 3 months) which pressures NIM, WTI crude at $98.38/bbl poses credit risk, and missing Q4 2025 data prevents full trend validation. The over-capitalized position (CET1 14.3%) and expected H2 2026 buyback acceleration provide a modest near-term catalyst, but regulatory uncertainty around Basel III endgame (~$20B additional capital) and G-SIB surcharges limits the re-rating path. Net: strong franchise + improving earnings + cheap valuation vs history warrants a mildly-to-moderately attractive score, held back by macro headwinds and leverage risk.
